clue.text: The day of the handyman

definitions.meaning: a day of the week, the one before Saturday
Man ..., Robinson Crusoe's servant, gave his name to any willing helper or general factotum

explanation.surface: A question of which weekday belongs to the odd-job man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from one name: a weekday, and Crusoe's servant whose name now means a general assistant.

clue.text: Navigator on the Canterbury road

definitions.meaning: Sir John ... was the Arctic explorer lost seeking the Northwest Passage
one of Chaucer's pilgrims telling tales on the way to Canterbury

explanation.surface: A sailor travelling along the road to Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a famous polar explorer and to a landowner among Chaucer's pilgrims.

clue.text: Home dream of childhood?

parts.note: in means at home
a fancy is a dream or daydream

explanation.surface: A dream of home recalled from early years.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest period of life, babyhood, is the start of childhood.

clue.text: Friendly as a fellow standing for the US Government

definitions.text: Friendly as a fellow standing for the US Government

parts.words: Friendly as a fellow standing for the US Government
parts.note: the fellow who personifies the American government is Uncle Sam, and kindly behaviour like his is uncle-like

explanation.surface: A political candidate in America being genial on the campaign trail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means kind and genial in the manner of an uncle, and Uncle Sam stands for the American state.

clue.text: Not a substance to give athletes, a heavenly body?

definitions.text: Not a substance to give athletes, a heavenly body?

parts.words: Not a substance to give athletes, a heavenly body?
parts.note: split one letter in, the word becomes 'a' plus a banned muscle-building drug; read whole, it is a small rocky body orbiting the sun

explanation.surface: A wry correction: the thing in question is a celestial object, not a performance-enhancing drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet is a small rocky body circling the sun, a heavenly body in the old phrase.

clue.text: Well placed to afford trip over the water

definitions.text: Well placed to afford trip over the water

parts.words: Well placed to afford trip over the water
parts.note: not wealthy enough for a holiday abroad, but rocks set at intervals so one can walk across a stream

explanation.surface: Someone financially comfortable enough to go abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat rocks placed in a stream let a walker cross without wading.

clue.text: Prefer voters not to speak

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the speaking from the voters

parts.note: the electorate is the body of voters
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Voters would rather stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose one option over another is to opt for it, as in 'elect to stay'.

clue.text: Shakespearian character who made Lamb work hard at first'

indicators.note: at first puts the work and hard ahead of the Lamb

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pen name Elia

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare heroine who drove Charles Lamb, author of Tales from Shakespeare, to toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's beloved, who drowns, is a character in one of Shakespeare's tragedies.

clue.text: City of Constantia; we're in Meredith!

definitions.text: City of Constantia; we're in Meredith!

parts.words: City of Constantia; we're in Meredith!
parts.note: Constantia is a character in George Meredith's novel The Egoist, and her surname is that of a cathedral city

explanation.surface: Sounds like a visitor hailing a town named Constantia from somewhere called Meredith.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city in north-east England shares its name with Constantia, the fiancée who jilts Sir Willoughby in The Egoist.

clue.text: Butcher chap with a blue apron is unfriendly

indicators.note: butcher as a verb means to mangle, so the letters are hacked into a new order

explanation.surface: A butcher in a blue apron who is unfriendly to customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' looks like the tradesman, but it is a verb here, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stand-offish and hard to approach is aloof and unfriendly.

clue.text: A chap like Fagin possessed by fever for riches

indicators.note: the fever is held inside the chap, as if he were possessed by it

parts.note: Fagin in Oliver Twist receives stolen goods, which makes him a fence
flu is an illness bringing fever

explanation.surface: A Dickensian rogue in the grip of a fever while chasing wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is wealth or abundance of money, the same as riches.

clue.text: Clear, blue sky beyond the clouds out there

definitions.text: Clear, blue sky beyond the clouds

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the five letters of 'there' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poetic gesture at the clear blue heavens up above the clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out there' reads as a place, but 'out' is the anagram signal working on THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: In old cosmology the upper regions of clear sky above the clouds were thought filled with a pure rarefied substance.

clue.text: A royal trophy with yellow flowers

definitions.note: the plural stands for the plant, which bears many blooms

parts.note: a king is a royal person
a cup is a typical trophy

explanation.surface: A regal prize decorated with golden blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh marigold, a buttercup relative of wet meadows, bears bright golden blooms.

clue.text: Father William given a bone

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
William Tell is the Swiss hero who shot an apple from his son's head

explanation.surface: A dad called William receives a bone, perhaps for his dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is a small flat bone at the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Piccadilly terminus transformed by picturesque scene

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged
the terminus of a word is its end, so only the closing stretch of Piccadilly is used

explanation.surface: The end of a London line is made over into a pretty rural view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminus' keeps DILLY, the end of Piccadilly (a famous London street and Tube line), and 'transformed' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a peaceful, charming pastoral scene, often idealised.

clue.text: The way of a man about town

definitions.text: The way of a man about town

parts.words: The way of a man about town
parts.note: not a sociable gadabout's habits but a road that literally goes round a town

explanation.surface: A remark on how a socialite behaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass circling a town lets traffic travel around it rather than through it.

clue.text: The might, say, of an angry eight-footer

definitions.text: The might, say, of an angry eight-footer

parts.words: The might, say, of an angry eight-footer
parts.note: might said aloud is mite, an eight-legged creature; angry suggests red, and eight-footer a spider

explanation.surface: Musing on how powerful an enraged spider might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny reddish mite that infests garden plants and greenhouses goes by this common name.

clue.text: People curse such clothing

parts.note: men are people
to swear is to curse

explanation.surface: Folk swear at certain garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments made for males are sold under this shop heading.

clue.text: They get a walk-over on entry

definitions.text: They get a walk-over on entry

parts.words: They get a walk-over on entry
parts.note: not easy sporting wins but mats at the door that people literally walk over as they come in

explanation.surface: Teams handed an easy victory at the start of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mats at a threshold are trodden on by everyone coming in; figuratively they are people others exploit.

clue.text: Time for revolution

parts.note: the month in whose name the 1917 Russian Bolshevik uprising is known

explanation.surface: A call to rise up now.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshevik seizure of power in 1917 is named after the tenth month of the old calendar.

clue.text: Writer reinstated in place of editor

annotationWithheld.clue: Writer reinstated in place of editor

clue.text: School of language?

parts.note: the word names both a school of painting from Flanders and the Dutch tongue spoken in Belgium

explanation.surface: A question about a language academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters such as Van Eyck form the Flanders school, and the Dutch spoken in northern Belgium is the language.

clue.text: A sign to note

parts.note: a printed mark such as a dagger used to point to a footnote or mark a doubtful passage

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay attention to a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This printer's mark, a dagger or division symbol, flags spurious passages or refers to notes.

clue.text: Make firm offer of a partnership

definitions.text: Make firm offer of a partnership

parts.words: Make firm offer of a partnership
parts.note: sounds like a business proposal, but the partnership is marriage and the offer a promise to wed

explanation.surface: A company tabling a formal bid to go into partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone formally to be married is a binding promise of a lifelong union.

clue.text: Ancient letter of days gone by

parts.note: old means ancient
en is the printer's name for the letter N

explanation.surface: An old letter from times past.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes former times, as in 'days of yore'.

clue.text: Shore up' building to — accommodate musician

indicators.note: building means constructing something new from the letters of 'Shore up'

explanation.surface: Propping up a building so it can house a resident player.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Greek lyre-player charmed beasts and stones with his music.

clue.text: Epithet for The Listener's launch by journalist

parts.note: to lob is to launch something high into the air
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A description of the debut of The Listener magazine, written up by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener was a BBC magazine, but here the listener is an ear, which has a fleshy lobe.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear has a lobe, so an adjective meaning having lobes fits it.

clue.text: Toast, perhaps, to mark free issue — queue for it

parts.note: toast is one example of bread
a line is a mark drawn on a surface

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to celebrate a free giveaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' suggests a drink to celebrate, but it is a kind of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor people once queued for free handouts of food, the original queue for charity loaves.

clue.text: Old magazine editor left in the lurch

parts.note: The Strand Magazine was a British monthly that first published Sherlock Holmes stories

explanation.surface: An editor of a defunct magazine abandoned by colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: To be left in the lurch is to be abandoned in difficulty, like a boat stuck on a shore.

clue.text: Such as Little John in band of twelve

definitions.meaning: Little John was a bowman in Robin Hood's band of outlaws
Sagittarius, the bowman, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac band

explanation.surface: Little John counted as one of a group of twelve men.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman is one who shoots arrows, as Robin Hood's men did; one zodiac sign shows such a bowman.
